name: Karnofsky Performance Status

version.label: Karnofsky Performance Status (Karnofsky 1949)
version.detail: 11 levels from 100 (normal) to 0 (dead) in steps of 10.

purpose: Describes functional performance, commonly in patients with cancer.

options.label: 100: Normal; no complaints; no evidence of disease
90: Able to carry on normal activity; minor signs or symptoms
80: Normal activity with effort; some signs or symptoms
70: Cares for self; unable to carry on normal activity or active work
60: Requires occasional assistance; cares for most needs
50: Requires considerable assistance and frequent medical care
40: Disabled; requires special care and assistance
30: Severely disabled; hospital care needed, death not imminent
20: Very sick; hospital care and active support needed

resultStates.label: KPS 100
resultStates.summary: Normal function with no complaints at this assessment.

resultStates.label: KPS {total}
resultStates.summary: Able to carry on normal activity and work.

resultStates.label: KPS {total}
resultStates.summary: Unable to work; lives at home and cares for most personal needs with varying assistance.

resultStates.label: KPS {total}
resultStates.summary: Unable to care for self; needs institutional or hospital-level care.

clinicalContext.text: A long-established performance scale used in oncology trials and prognostic scores (e.g. Tokuhashi).

clinicalInsights.text: ECOG is an alternative performance scale; conversions between them are approximate.

limitations: Reflects all causes of impairment, not only cancer.

guideSections.whenToUse: Describing functional performance, especially in oncology.
guideSections.howToPerform: Select the level that best matches current function.
guideSections.clinicalContext: One input to multidisciplinary oncology decisions.

sources.citation: Karnofsky DA, Burchenal JH. The clinical evaluation of chemotherapeutic agents in cancer. In: MacLeod CM, ed. Evaluation of Chemotherapeutic Agents. Columbia University Press; 1949:191-205.
